sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $23.7 billion to $51.8 billion [F1][F10][F168].
The path was cyclical rather than steady: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 before a 20.5% drop in FY2023 [D161][D200][D238][D274].
The FY2023 decline came from lower realized commodity prices partly offset by higher sales volumes [P47].
Net income swung from a $3.6 billion loss in FY2016 to $18.7 billion in FY2022, then fell to $8.0 billion in FY2025 [F11][F17][F20].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth that year [D382][D384][D342].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but added only 0.1pp to growth, while natural gas liquids grew 28.2% and added 1.5pp [D551][D553][D665][D666].
FY2025 sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 while revenue rose 4.9%, and basic EPS fell 18.7% against that net income decline [D343][D342][D344].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% in FY2025, faster than the 4.9% revenue growth [D352][D342].
Net margin of 15.4% in FY2025 sat below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, with the 36.9% effective tax rate above the 32.4% of FY2024 [D351][D332][D298].
DD&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025 on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
SG&A fell $265 million in FY2025 on the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses, partly offset by restructuring severance [P23].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.18x of FY2024 [F59][F20][D333][D299].
The FY2025 operating cash flow decrease from FY2024 came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].
Operating cash flow was 33.6% of revenue in FY2025, and stock-based compensation was 1.7% of operating cash flow [D331][D334].
Capex of $10.2 billion in FY2022 was 1.35x D&A and 12.9% of revenue [F66][D228][D222].
Net cash of $7.1 billion was 12.1% of revenue in FY2025, the 100th percentile against a -7.7% peer median (n=6) [D337][D338][D850][D851].

FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capex and investments, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sale proceeds [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, against the stated framework of returning more than 30% [D339][P31].
The diluted share count rose 6.1% in FY2025, reversing the 2.1% decline of FY2024 [D356][D322].
Revenue in the table is a later recast for every year: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons that mix a recast year with a first-reported year are not like-for-like, so the 9.1% CAGR should be read with that caveat [F168].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023, the only decline in the last four years [F8][D274].
That drop was price-driven rather than volume-driven, so it reflects commodity exposure rather than a loss of operating position [P47].
Whether net margin holds above the 17.9% window median or falls toward the 15.4% FY2025 level will show in the FY2026 10-K [D831][F30].
Whether operating cash flow stays above the $19.8 billion FY2025 level or slips toward the $20.0 billion FY2023 figure will appear in the FY2026 cash flow statement [F59][F57].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue holds near 12.1% or falls toward the 11.2% FY2024 level will show in the FY2026 balance sheet [D338][D304].
